business_problem: Changan Automobile needed far more HPC capacity for CAE-based vehicle R&D as model counts, simulation domains, and bursty demand kept growing, but self-built clusters could not keep up with the required scale, upgrade cycle, or cost flexibility.
solution_summary: Tencent Cloud worked with Changan's global R&D center to move CAE simulation workloads onto an elastic cloud HPC architecture. Engineers can upload simulation files, choose solvers, and set configuration parameters on Tencent's platform instead of waiting for fixed on-premises cluster capacity. The environment combines Tencent Cloud's high-performance computing platform with Intel Ice Lake and AMD EPYC instances, a RoCE V2 100G RDMA network for microsecond latency, A100 and A10 GPU resource pools, and a shared parallel file system with up to 100 GB/s throughput. Tencent adapted the platform for different CAE software packages and kept refreshing the compute generation year by year, so crash, NVH, multibody, fluid, combustion, and electromagnetic simulations could burst on demand while Changan paid through a mix of subscription, pay-as-you-go, and spot-style pricing rather than overbuilding local infrastructure.

solution_components.name: Tencent Cloud High-Performance Computing Platform
solution_components.role: Allocates and manages elastic compute capacity for Changan's CAE simulation workloads.

solution_components.name: RoCE V2 100G RDMA network
solution_components.role: Provides the low-latency fabric that links simulation nodes for tightly coupled HPC jobs.

solution_components.name: A100/A10 GPU resource pool
solution_components.role: Supplies burstable accelerated compute for simulation and engineering analysis workloads.

solution_components.name: parallel file system
solution_components.role: Stores and serves shared simulation inputs and outputs at high throughput for concurrent jobs.

data_flow: Changan engineers upload CAE files and choose solvers and configuration parameters on Tencent Cloud. Jobs are scheduled onto elastic CPU and GPU pools connected by the RoCE V2 RDMA fabric, read and write shared datasets through the parallel file system, and return simulation results to Changan's vehicle R&D teams for design validation and iteration.
integration_points: Crash, NVH, multibody, fluid, combustion, and electromagnetic simulation pipelines
business_outcome: Changan gained continuously refreshed compute generations, elastic HPC capacity, and flexible pricing for CAE workloads, helping the automaker scale simulation-led R&D faster without carrying the same upgrade and overprovisioning burden of a self-built cluster.
